text: PHILIP MORRIS PRODUCTS INC.
TOBACCO TECHNOLOGY GROUP
RECEIVED
INTER-OFFICECORRESPONDENCE
Richmond, Virginia
Ken Houghton
To:
K. S. Houghton
Date: May 19, 1988
From:
D. P. O'Brien
Subject: FML
Dear Ken,
I understand from a conversation with Charlie Bates that the need
for any current activity on the FML project within R&D is somewhat
unclear to you. I will recap the position as follows:
Following from your presentation to B. Murray in which you
expressed USA's view that the FML filter was unsuitable for PM USA
projects, I have decided, in agreement with G. Bible, to relocate
the plug-making activities to FML London with a target date of
July 1. This will require the transfer of the KDF-2/AF-1, which is
in the process of being modified, and the MK-6/Mini. In the
meantime some sample plug-making commitments will be required
in order to initiate the program of market tests overseas that has
been decided upon by PMI.
Irrespective of PM USA's plans, the development program for FML for
1988, which was agreed and funded, requires the development of the
rod-making activity to 400 meters/minute on a KDF-2. This work has
been substantially completed and some limited re-engineering and
speed trials remain to be conducted.
I would ask your cooperation in ensuring that this work continues
with urgency until July 1. The mechanisms are already in place by
which the charges for this assistance are transferred to FML, and I
understand that currently W. Nichols and D. Laslie are charged in
total.
You will be aware that Walt's involvement is at a low level, but I
understand that D. Laslie's work does not conflict with other
priorities. Since the FML project will be handled exclusively in
London and through the TTG from the first of July onwards, I would
request that the project records and files compiled by W. Nichols
during his involvement be made available by July lst for transfer
to London in order to ensure continuity.
